plan.summary: Mechanical fabrication gate for tool-recreation-handler (bug 020), now WITH its wiring. A new local action check_tool_fabrication inspects the generated tool; on a fabrication signature it returns fabricated=true, and a new conditional step routes the item to needs_human_review (via the existing checkpoint_for_review) instead of deploying. Tiered detection keeps it precise: Tier A (declared synthetic data, or introduced synthetic-PII generators) fires alone; Tier B (seeded PRNG / corpus builder / >=2 crossed fragment arrays / large literal record array) fires only when corroborated by the exact bug-020 signature — the original was data-backed AND the recreation dropped the fetch. The Go action is inert until an image roll; the workflow wiring (edit 5) is applied image-first (after the pod carries the action).

edits.rationale: Pure, DB-free core so the precision logic is fully unit-testable. Tier A fires alone (self-declaration of synthetic data near a data noun; makePostcode/randomPhone-style PII generators the recreation INTRODUCED that the original lacked). Tier B fires only when corroborated: a corpus signature AND the original was data-backed (a data-ish fetch/XHR, or analysis data_source.has_external_data) AND the recreation preserves no fetch of its own. Corroboration spares a dice game or a name-generator tool.
edits.sketch: tierA := selfDeclaration || (syntheticPII(rec) && !syntheticPII(orig)); if tierA {tier=declaration}; else corpus := prng||builder||>=2 fragmentArrays||>=15 recordObjects; if corpus && (analysisDataBacked||originalDataFetch(orig)) && !anyFetch(rec) {tier=corroborated_corpus}.

edits.rationale: Wrapper reads the generated HTML, original source and analysis data_source from collected_data and runs DetectToolFabrication. FIELD PATHS VERIFIED against the live tool-recreation-handler workflow: completeness_check.clean_html is exactly what validate_tool reads (check_completeness.output_field=completeness_check); existing_content.existing_content.raw_html and tool_analysis.result are both referenced verbatim by the recreate_tool prompt. Fails OPEN on missing HTML (the completeness step owns empty output) so the gate never becomes a fleet-wide recreation blocker.
edits.sketch: recreation := ExtractNestedFieldString(cd, 'completeness_check.clean_html'); original := ...'existing_content.existing_content.raw_html'; res := DetectToolFabrication(recreation, original, dataSourceIsExternal(cd['tool_analysis.result.data_source'])); return {fabricated,tier,signals,detail}

edits.rationale: Register the action beside check_tool_completeness. Purely additive: the registry is a name->Handler map read by dispatch; nothing enumerates its keys exhaustively (no switch/enum over registry contents), so a new key cannot perturb existing pipelines — mirrors the check_tool_completeness registration exactly.

11 tests pinning the precision contract (renamed to _action_test.go to match the source file, per round-2 editquality). The real vetcomparison fabrication is gated both WITH the confessing comment (Tier A) and with it removed (Tier B). A dice game, a calculator, a faithful fetch-preserving recreation, an honest empty state, and a name-generator tool are NOT gated. Tests use hand-built payloads; the field-path correctness that the real context depends on is verified separately (edit 2 rationale).

THE deploy-blocking guarantee (round-2 editquality HIGH). Owning pipeline: tool-recreation-handler. Inserts check_fabrication after check_completeness, then a conditional route_fabrication: on fabrication_check.fabricated==true it goes to request_fabrication_review (checkpoint_for_review, raising a needs_human_review item carrying the generated HTML + signals) and then complete — it NEVER reaches save_sections/update_status(deployed)/deploy_page. On false it goes to save_training_data (the original next step). Applied IMAGE-FIRST: the step names check_tool_fabrication, which must be in the pod first (verified by pod-grep before applying).
edits.sketch: check_completeness.next_step: save_training_data -> check_fabrication; check_fabrication -> route_fabrication (conditional 'fabrication_check.fabricated == true' ? request_fabrication_review : save_training_data); request_fabrication_review (checkpoint_for_review, item_type=needs_human_review, severity=high) -> complete. Fabricated tools never reach save_sections/deploy_page.

plan.risks: 1) Wiring correctness (edit 5) is the real deploy-blocking guarantee and is NOT covered by the Go unit tests — confirm the conditional routes fabricated=true to checkpoint_for_review and that neither save_sections nor deploy_page is reachable on that branch. 2) FALSE POSITIVES on legit tools -> held for human review (not silent breakage); mitigated by the Tier B corroboration gate and 6 negative unit tests. 3) FALSE NEGATIVE: a fabrication that fetches a decoy URL reads as 'preserved' — a follow-up could require the preserved fetch to hit the SAME source. 4) Image-first ordering: edit 5 must be applied only after a pod-grep confirms check_tool_fabrication is in the running binary (documented in the RUNBOOK and the wiring header).
